description.narrative: The Upazilas of Cox’s Bazar are geographically one of the most vulnerable areas and are prone to climate-induced shocks. Every year, natural disasters like cyclones, floods, storm surges, landslides, etc. happen, and severe loss and damage to the natural resources, infrastructure, livelihoods, death, and injury are observed. As the areas are relatively vulnerable and mostly consist of the reserve forest areas, a non-durable infrastructure development focusing on nature-based solutions is the only measure where risk mitigation and resilience building can be ensured along with the accessibility to the food security and nutrition of the vulnerable communities. Throughout these initiatives, the natural resources management initiative can be ensured on a broader scale and in a sustainable way. Following the key identified needs through our current ongoing interventions and the updated needs assessment collective done by Christian Aid and local partner GUK, the proposed activities in camps include: 1) Climate resilient nature-based site improvement activities at all proposed camps (22-27 and NRC) 2) Drainage cleaning in camps 22-27 and NRC, 3) Reforestation in all the proposed camps (both plantation and care and maintenance) and 4) Fire prevention and response in all camps (22-27 and NRC). The proposed local community interventions include Reforestation (both plantation and care and maintenance) (The areas with specific needs consulting with Bangladesh Forest Division, under these 2 upazilas) and awareness Programs targeting community-led actions in all the proposed camps.
